comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD define their primary Data Center computing segments to include AI accelerators. NVDA's Compute & Networking segment is defined broadly to include the 'Data Center accelerated computing platform' alongside networking and automotive solutions, as seen in the citation. AMD explicitly lists 'Data Center' as a reportable segment that 'primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs)...'. While both focus on the data center AI infrastructure market, NVDA's segment definition is more holistic, encompassing networking and software (NVIDIA AI Enterprise, DGX Cloud), whereas AMD's segment definition in this specific sentence isolates the hardware components (CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, etc.) within the Data Center bucket.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment includes our Data Center accelerated computing platform; networking; automotive artificial intelligence, or AI, Cockpit, autonomous driving development agreements, and autonomous vehicle solutions; electric vehicle computing platforms; Jetson for robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud.

• the Data Center segment, which primarily includes Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators, server microprocessors (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), accelerated processing units (APUs), data processing units (DPUs), Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) and Adaptive System-on-Chip (SoC) products for data centers;
